Chapter 1883: Duty And Personal Affection (I)

Western Curtain Sea.

Bright moonlight shone over the rolling sea, layers of radiance reflected upon its surface. Suddenly, divine abilities shimmered and rippled through the air, revealing two Daoist Masters, one behind the other.

The one in front wore Daoist robes, with three brocade pouches tied at his waist. He carried a long staff resembling green bamboo over his shoulder. Several small jade swords hung loosely from its end, clinking brightly against one another.

His attire was rather unusual. Middle-aged in appearance, he had a reddish complexion and a solemn expression. His eyes were half-closed in thought.

An old man followed behind him, his splendid clothes neatly arranged. Yet his face was deathly pale, and his eyes betrayed the pain of a costly expenditure. When the man ahead remained silent for a long while, he finally spoke.

"Fellow Daoist Xie...?"

The Daoist Master he addressed seemed to come to his senses. He let out a long breath. "Senior... this is truly extraordinary!

"The shamanic talismans within that cave dwelling are extraordinary, and so is the secret realm itself... If someone inside possessed sufficient Dao conduct, they could even use it to evade or drive back enemies... In fact, I suspect the entire cave dwelling could be gathered up and taken away!"

The two were none other than Yan Dushui and Xiehu!

The Western Sea lay so far from the Western Curtain Sea that, while the Li Family had long since finished its business, these two seemed to have only just visited the cave dwelling. Daoist Master Xiehu's eyes were slightly red.

Deeply moved, he asked, "May I ask... what exactly did the great figure your ancestor encountered look like?"

Yan Dushui fell silent at this. After a long while, he said, "For generations, my family has suspected he came from the Underworld. Yet the word he used at the time was 'immortal'..."

Xiehu's expression grew grave. "I fear this figure does not belong to the Three Profundities.

"My Dao lineage cultivates the Shamanic Talisman Dao, and our inheritance goes back many generations. My grandmaster once exchanged insights with Duanmu Kui, and had some friendship with him. He also knew a fair amount about the inheritances of the Three Profundities and the Shamanic Talisman Dao.

"I do not know whether this senior belongs to the Underworld's judiciary. Even if he does, he originally followed a Dao outside the Three Profundities, became a ghost, and joined the judiciary."

Though Yan Dushui had guarded this treasured land for years, his family followed neither Supreme Shaman nor Merging Owl. He could not discern its mysteries and had little interest in them.

After listening, he sighed. "I only hope it can be of some help to you, fellow Daoist..."

Xiehu had a complicated expression, half joyful and half sorrowful, as he replied, "Help... that is difficult to say. My grandmaster once discussed the profound Dao with Duanmu Kui. That Daoist Master, renowned throughout north and south, once said, 'Supreme Shaman seems vacant, but is in truth obscured. It exists merely to answer banishment. If I were to attain its Dao, I fear it would cost me my life.'"

Though he lived far away, Yan Dushui had heard of Duanmu Kui. He paused in surprise. "I heard he was overbearing and headstrong, boasting that he had received an immortal's guidance and wielding immense power. But even he said something like that?"

"Immortals... There is more than one immortal. If the Underworld's judiciary had none, how could it have endured from ancient times until now?" Xiehu's expression dimmed as he continued, "My grandmaster advised him, 'The immortal said you could attain a Golden Position, but must it be that of Supreme Shaman? The Surplus and Intercalary Positions remain above. Look to them with hope.'

"But you are right. That senior was headstrong and domineering. He pursued that sole path all the way to his death. If even someone as formidable as him... could not attain the Dao... who else in the world would dare try?"

The middle-aged man turned to Yan Dushui and thanked him solemnly. "The supreme profound talismans inscribed in your cave dwelling convey profound truths in the simplest strokes. I have benefited greatly from them. Yet however extraordinary they may be, they cannot compare with that immortal text. If even Duanmu Kui failed, what could I accomplish? I cultivate Supreme Shaman, but the Dao I seek lies beyond it. These talismans cannot help me attain that Dao!"

Yan Dushui stood speechless for a long while, bitterness welling in his heart. Then Xiehu changed tack, lowering his eyes as he said, "But with that wall of profound talismans, I can cross the Purple Mansion Threshold! That is an immense kindness indeed!"

Only then did the old man breathe out in relief and say happily, "That is good... That is good!"

Filled with joy, he was already planning how to send Li Ximing the good news and make the most of what Xiehu had revealed in this brief exchange.

Seeing the old man's deathly pale face as he continued murmuring to himself, pity flickered in Xiehu's eyes. He said softly, "I know what you seek, senior. But... seeking the Dao through your own efforts and roaming freely through heaven and earth is the true path of immortal cultivation. Why place your hopes in your descendants? That is misguided. You do possess divine abilities, after all. If you wish, I can use certain Shamanic Talisman Dao arts to dissolve those divine abilities and give you a few more decades of life... Perhaps another opportunity will arise?"

Yan Dushui had been beaming at his earlier words, but the latter part made him turn and stare at Xiehu. Seeing the man standing beneath the moonlight, brimming with confidence, the old man replied with a smile, "Without your grandmaster, how could you seek the Dao through your own efforts and roam freely through heaven and earth today? Whether it is a Dao lineage or one's descendants, this is no shirking of responsibility. It is helping others fulfill their potential, and it is no less worthy than your pursuit of the Dao. Clinging to life serves no purpose. If I cannot attain the Dao myself, then let those in whom I place my hopes attain it!"

Xiehu watched him quietly. The old man's divine sense was already dissipating, the essence of his mana wavering and drawing snow down around them. Yet his face remained full of smiles, his words firm and resonant. Xiehu nodded solemnly and brought his hands together. "I have learned from you, senior."

Simin.

Dawn was breaking, and the streets had grown cold again. The rumble of wheels echoed before the entrance as a young man in dark robes alighted from his carriage. The crimson gates swung open, and a boy came running out.

The boy had delicate features and light steps, with deep golden light in his eyes. Smiling excitedly, he stopped before the gate and looked up at the young man. "Fourth uncle... You're back from court!"

A smile immediately spread across Li Jiangliang's face. Taking the boy's small hand, he said, "It's your birthday, Suichu. I haven't forgotten..."

From his green-black sleeve, he took a walnut-sized bead that shone brilliantly. The boy accepted it with delight, and they went inside together. At the entrance to the inner courtyard stood a girl, hiding behind the doorway with only half her face showing. She smiled shyly at him.

"Fourth uncle..."

Her smile was expectant, her eyes fixed on his sleeve. Li Jiangliang's smile broadened as he took out a palm-sized mirror. "I haven't forgotten you, Zhi'er![1]"

The girl accepted it with shining eyes and thanked him politely before gathering up her hem to chase her brother. Li Jiangliang watched with a smile as the two children played their way out of sight down the corridor, then entered the courtyard.

His elder brother wore a plain, unlined robe with both sleeves rolled up. Holding a small pair of white jade shears, he studied the plum blossoms in a porcelain vase. Pink petals lay scattered around him.

Li Jiangliang approached and bowed. Li Jiangxia smiled and said, "You've gone to such trouble... arranging my transfer back to the capital so I wouldn't miss these two little ones' birthdays. Suichu is easier to please, but Zhi'er is much harder to coax..."

The brothers were clearly much closer than when they had first entered court service. Li Jiangliang replied, "Both children are close to you and gentle by nature. Lady Zou[2] has raised them well."

Li Jiangxia led him to a seat and shook his head. "You're mistaken there. Suichu is mischievous, and nowhere near as steady as Suihuan. Li Jianglong may have little else worth mentioning, but he certainly excels at fathering children. That is the one thing I envy about him."

1. Referring to Li Yuzhi, daughter of Li Jiangxia, twin sister of Li Suichu. ☜

2. Referring to Zuo Xie, a concubine of Li Jiangxia. ☜
